newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus names new bank head amid corruption charge.
newsitem.headline: Belarus names new bank head amid corruption charge.

text.p: Belarus appointed an acting central bank chief on Wednesday after his predecessor was sacked and arrested in connection with a corruption charge.
State television said the new acting head was Nikolai Korbut, until now deputy to Tamara Vinnikova.
State radio said on Tuesday that Vinnikova had been detained and was accused of "damage to the state of major proportions".
Little is known about Korbut, who had rarely spoken out in public before being appointed to the post, which is directly controlled by President Alexander Lukashenko.
On Wednesday Korbut told state television he understood that the charges against Vinnikova were connected to her activities before she joined the central bank last February.
She once headed the Belarus Bank, which merged with the state savings bank in August 1995 to create the largest bank in the country of 10 million.
Vinnikova had initially been an unquestioning supporter of Lukashenko's reluctant approach to market reforms, but over time objected to many of his policies.
She opposed Lukashenko's decision to lower refinancing rates without consulting the central bank and the creation of a corridor to regulate the rate of the Belarussian rouble.

Russia's Interfax news agency quoted an unnamed source at the former Soviet republic's prosecutor's office as saying Vinnikova was arrested because of "abuse of her position and financial machinations".
The alleged irregularities were uncovered during checks of financial activities at Belarusbank instigated by Lukashenko himself, Interfax quoted the source as saying.
It quoted the source as saying that more than 30 percent of credits at Belarusbank were to false companies which only existed for 24 hours, and that the money had since vanished.
Interfax said it was alleged that the equivalent of $10 million of investors' money was used for the bank's own needs, like renting office space and buying cars and computers.
Vinnikova, 46, was being detained and would be charged officially on Thursday, Interfax quoted the source as saying.
Vinnikova's arrest and sacking came on a day when Finance Minister Pavel Dik resigned, though the two events did not appear to be linked.
The resignation followed a string of changes in Lukashenko's cabinet in recent months.
Lukashenko has sacked or accepted the resignations of several ministers and top officials recently, particularly since winning a controversial constitutional referendum in November.
